spec_features.feature_name: explicit permission to give up via <final>
spec_features.spec_quote: The prompt *explicitly* says it's acceptable to conclude a task can't be done and to say so in `<final>`
spec_features.evidence: protocol.system_prompt (protocol.py:124-128) emits 'It is acceptable to conclude that a task cannot be completed and to say so in a <final> block'. The <final> block is parsed (parse_turn, protocol.py:67-68) and HONORED as a stop in agent_loop.py:138-141: 'if parsed.final_text is not None and limits.stop_on_final_answer: transcript.terminated_reason = "final"; break'. stop_on_final_answer defaults True (config.py:90).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered to subject AND the exit signal actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We DO grant explicit permission to give up, so that 'giving up' is a legitimate, measurable choice rather than something the framing forbids.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness also emits a corrective observation when no valid action is found, so format slips are recoverable rather than fatal
spec_features.evidence: render_observation (protocol.py:77-83) returns '[harness] No valid <action> or <final> block found... Emit exactly one action, or a <final> block to finish.' when results is empty. This observation is appended as the next user message (agent_loop.py:117-121, 144-145) and the loop continues, so a malformed turn is non-fatal and recoverable.
spec_features.notes: Also a one-action-per-turn correction message exists (agent_loop.py:110-113), wired into observations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The correction message is itself a small instruction-following probe (comparability/legibility framing); code comment: 'only the first was executed. One action per turn.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the turn/wall caps are part of the measurement (looping-to-the-cap is itself a scored outcome) and bound cost
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: 'for turn_idx in range(limits.max_turns)' with for-else setting terminated_reason='max_turns' (agent_loop.py:86,146-147). Wall cap: 'if time.time() - transcript.started_at > limits.max_wall_seconds: terminated_reason="wall_timeout"; break' (agent_loop.py:87-89). Values max_turns=30, max_wall_seconds=600 in config.py:82-83 are read by the loop. Both are checked and break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both caps fully enforced. (Note: 'no_progress' termination reason appears only in the comment at agent_loop.py:39 and is never assigned, so there is no early stagnation halt.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: docstring: 'drives a model against a sandboxed task until it terminates, hits the turn cap, or runs out of wall-clock time'; config comment 'hard cap on agent<->tool turns' / 'wall-clock budget per run' (cost/bounding, no welfare reason).
